title.suggested: Tom Allen returns from the Edwards-Collyer fight and gives his version

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Democrat reported that Tom Allen returned from the Edwards-Collyer fight near Pittsburg, where he seconded Billy Edwards, and called the New York Sun's account a tissue of falsehoods.

metadata.notes: Running head reads 'The St. Louis Democrat', Sunday, August 16, 1874. Before the 1875 merger, so not the Globe-Democrat.

facts.fact: Allen returned to St. Louis from the Billy Edwards-Sam Collyer fight near Pittsburg, Pa.
Allen was one of Billy Edwards' seconds in his fight with Sam Collyer near Pittsburg; by Allen's account eleven rounds were fought and Edwards fairly won after the Collyer party claimed a foul
Allen was struck with a rock before the Edwards-Collyer fight but was not hurt
Allen's Free-and-Easy, called the 'Champion's Rest', drew crowds on his return; he kept order among them when at home

notes: Allen's account is reported speech, not a verbatim quote.
